status_summary: S. 999, the Public Health Improvement Act, introduced 2025-03-12 and referred to the Senate HELP Committee, would amend section 319 of the Public Health Service Act so that renewals of a public health emergency require a majority vote of both chambers of Congress and last no more than 90 days after that vote. The GovInfo bill status record shows no action on S. 999 after referral, and no enacted law setting a fixed time frame for public health emergency declarations was found. The Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act remained unreauthorized as of 2026-02-16 per a state health officials association.

timeline.event: S. 999, the Public Health Improvement Act, was introduced and referred to the Senate HELP Committee; section 6 would make public health emergency renewals depend on a majority vote of both chambers and cap each renewal at 90 days.

title: Set a fixed time frame for public health emergency declarations with Secretary burden
uncertainties: Review found and read the introduced text of S. 999 on GovInfo; it requires congressional approval for renewals rather than a Secretary justification, so the match is partial, and it keeps the 48-hour notice to Congress. Congress.gov was not available; the GovInfo bill status record for S. 999 (updated 2026-01-06), read in review on 2026-10-17, shows only introduction and referral to the HELP Committee on 2025-03-12, one original cosponsor and no hearing, markup or floor action. Section 6 sets no new limit on an initial declaration and does not require the Secretary to justify an extension; continuation depends on a congressional vote. No House companion was searched. A 90-day automatic termination bill announced on 2024-01-26 predates the period; whether it was reintroduced in the 119th Congress was not found. The PAHPA status rests on a state health officials association post of 2026-02-16; later status was not checked.
